claims.sentence: On 27 July 2026 the WHO published a progress assessment of its 2022 to 2030 strategies on HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections.
claims.evidence: News item dated 27-07-2026; WHO 2026 mid-term progress report on the global health sector strategies 2022-2030.

claims.sentence: The WHO published the assessment on 27 July 2026.
claims.evidence: URL date 27-07-2026 and publication page "2026 mid-term progress report".

claims.sentence: The WHO names integration of services into primary health care as one of the biggest opportunities to speed progress.
claims.evidence: Headline: "Integration, innovation and community leadership key"; report identifies integration as one of the greatest opportunities to accelerate progress.

claims.sentence: It points to better diagnostics, quality-assured testing for sexually transmitted infections and long-acting prevention such as twice-yearly lenacapavir.
claims.evidence: Twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir is named (and rollout in 10 countries). Better diagnostics and quality-assured STI testing were not seen in any retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: It points to long-acting prevention such as twice-yearly lenacapavir.

claims.sentence: On 27 July 2026 the World Health Organization (WHO) published a progress assessment of its Global Health Sector Strategies on HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections for 2022 to 2030.
claims.evidence: Publication page: "Global health sector strategies on HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections, 2022-2030: 2026 mid-term progress report", news dated 27 July 2026.

claims.sentence: The WHO says integration is one of the biggest opportunities to speed progress, and that countries with the strongest results deliver HIV, hepatitis and STI care through primary health care.
claims.evidence: "Countries reporting the strongest results are increasingly delivering services for HIV, viral hepatitis and STIs through primary health care"; integration one of the greatest opportunities.

claims.sentence: It also points to innovation, including better diagnostics, quality-assured STI testing and long-acting prevention such as twice-yearly lenacapavir, and to stronger community leadership and community-generated data.
claims.evidence: Lenacapavir, community leadership and community-generated data are in the retrieved text. "Better diagnostics" and "quality-assured STI testing" were not found.
claims.newSentence: It also points to innovation, including long-acting prevention such as twice-yearly lenacapavir, and to stronger community leadership and community-generated data.

claims.sentence: The WHO released consolidated HIV service delivery guidelines and HIV surveillance guidance alongside the assessment, to help countries plan prevention, testing, treatment and care.
claims.evidence: Consolidated HIV service delivery guidelines are dated 22 July 2026; the surveillance guidance is dated 27 July 2026. "Released alongside the assessment" overstates the timing for the first, and the purpose clause was not seen in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: The WHO issued consolidated HIV service delivery guidelines (22 July 2026) and consolidated guidance on routine HIV surveillance (27 July 2026) in the same period.

claims.sentence: It says eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B remains a priority, with more countries applying for WHO validation.
claims.evidence: "Eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B remains a key priority"; a growing number of countries are applying for WHO validation.

notes: Dates for the two companion documents differ (22 vs 27 July); check whether the news item itself says "alongside". Publication page and news item blended in search summaries; text not read directly (WebFetch blocked).
